subject: Async job closure semaphore proposal and dedupe flow
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@atlaspayments.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: [Atlas] Nightly batch finalization misses + ask about SLA tolerance

Hi Tessa,

We saw a spike in nightly batch jobs failing to reach FINALIZED state between 02:00-03:30 PST for three consecutive nights (12/12-12/14). The jobs themselves complete, but Atlas's downstream system expects a FINALIZED callback within a 45-minute window; when that doesn't happen, we generate reconciles and double-submit transactions.

Can Redwood provide a temporary tolerance for the job-finalization window or propose a mitigation we can accept in contract? We need to avoid duplicates and ensure idempotency during the window. Attaching our latest observability snapshot.

Thanks,
Samir Rao
Sr. SRE | AtlasPayments
attachments: batch_observability_report_20271214.pdf

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Samir Rao <samir@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Dec 2027 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: [Atlas] Nightly batch finalization misses + ask about SLA tolerance

Samir — thanks for the report and the attachment. I reviewed the observability snapshot; we can see the long-tail finalizations coincide with GC pauses on a small subset of Dedicated nodes and with a spike in concurrent finalization requests from Atlas's ingestion window.

Immediate proposal:
- Short-term: Redwood can grant a 60-minute "finalization hedge" for the affected nightly window (Dec 12-20) while we deploy a mitigation. This would mean we accept credits only if finalization exceeds 60 minutes beyond the contract window.
- Mitigation: introduce a lightweight finalization semaphore to limit concurrency for downstream closure work + idempotency enforcement via per-job 128-bit idempotency tokens. The semaphore will gate the finalization step so we avoid thundering-herd retries.

Can we schedule a 30-min call to align on the operational details and sign off on the temporary hedge? If you prefer, we can also propose contract language for an amendment.

Thanks — Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Dec 2027 12:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: [Atlas] Nightly batch finalization misses + ask about SLA tolerance

Looping in Karthik for infra/arch input. A few quick notes:
- Semaphore idea: implement a per-tenant finalization token bucket with a soft cap of N concurrent finalizations (configurable per account). That prevents the spike but preserves throughput overall.
- Idempotency: use client-provided idempotency token + server-side dedupe window of 7 days for batch job finalization events; accept a CRC fingerprint to detect payload-equivalent replays.
- Retry behavior: exponential backoff with jitter for finalization attempts, plus a safe-retry header so Atlas can surface retries to their reconciliation system.

We can prototype in staging tonight and roll to canary tomorrow. Tessa — if you get customer OK on the 60-min temporary hedge, we should draft the amendment and the Runbook updates.

—Ben

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Dec 2027 15:37:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: [Atlas] Nightly batch finalization misses + ask about SLA tolerance

Design notes from infra:
- Semaphore implementation: use a lightweight distributed semaphore backed by Redis for Dedicated pools with a fallback to token-queueing on Private. Config knobs: max_concurrent_finalizers, acquire_timeout_ms (we'll propose 30000ms), and priority for retrying jobs older than 24 hours.
- Dedupe: store an entry per job-id + CRC in our hot-key store for 7 days; if a duplicate attempt arrives, respond 200 with header X-Redwood-Dupe: true and a payload explaining time of original finalize. That avoids reprocessing.
- Observability: emit metrics finalizer.queue_depth, finalizer.acquire_latency_ms, finalizer.duplicate_reject_count. We'll also add a short-lived alert rule to page on acquire_latency > 2000ms during the nightly window.

I'll stand up a staging branch and push a draw.io diagram for the flow (proposed_dedupe_flow.drawio) to the shared Drive. If legal wants contract text, I can seed language for the amendment.

-Karthik

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Samir Rao <samir@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 16 Dec 2027 16:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: [Atlas] Nightly batch finalization misses + ask about SLA tolerance

Samir — quick follow-up with what we agreed internally and the customer-facing ask: 

Summary of proposed compensation and mitigation:
- Temporary finalization hedge: Redwood will accept a one-time deviation tolerance of up to 60 minutes for the nightly window Dec 12–20. During this period, we will not trigger SLA credits for finalization delays that fall within that hedge.
- Operational mitigation: deploy per-tenant finalization semaphore and 7-day idempotency/dedupe store. Expected reduction in duplicate reconciles: ~95% for the problematic pattern seen in your snapshot.
- Rollout plan: prototype in staging today -> canary for 5% of traffic tomorrow -> full Dedicated rollout by 12/19.
- Runbook & observability: we will provide an updated runbook and alerts for acquire_latency and duplicate counts.

Next steps:
1) Can you confirm Atlas accepts the temporary hedge (Dec 12–20, 60 minutes)? Reply with OK and I’ll draft an amendment and the runbook.
2) If you want tighter guarantees later, we can propose a contract amendment for an SLA carveout with a credit schedule tied to finalizer.acquire_latency_ms.

Appreciate the quick sync — want to get this in motion before your next nightly run.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
